data.title: Belite Bio drops on FDA review extension for tinlarebant NDA
data.description:
• Belite Bio (BLTE) is down ~13% Friday after the US FDA said it would delay by three months the PDUFA date for the company's NDA for tinlarebant for Stargardt disease type 1.
  • The new action date is May 12, 2027.
  • The company noted that the agency said that if no major issues are found during the ongoing review, it will communicate proposed labeling requests and any anticipated postmarketing requirement requests by April 12.
  • Tinlarebant is an oral treatment designed to reduce the accumulation of vitamin A-based toxins, known as bisretinoids, that cause retinal disease in Stargardt disease type 1.

data.title: Hewlett Packard Q4 preview: What to expect
data.description:
Analysts expect Hewlett Packard (HPE) to benefit from healthy enterprise infrastructure spending, strong networking demand, and improving storage trends when it reports fourth-quarter earnings on November 23rd, after the closing bell.

The consensus EPS estimate is $1.29, while the consensus revenue estimate is $14.43B—falling within management’s raised guidance range of $1.20 and $1.30 and $13.9 billion and $14.8 billion, respectively.

Heading into the earnings, analysts at Citi saw a constructive setup for enterprise hardware providers like HPE and Dell (DELL) on the back of pent-up enterprise infrastructure demand, healthy AI backlogs, and operational/supply-chain efficiencies to navigate volatility.

Ahead of the earnings, analysts are bullish about the firm, with EPS estimates seeing 17 upward revisions and revenue estimates seeing 15 upward moves over the last 3 months, with neither witnessing any downward adjustments.

A large part of this optimism is being driven by the networking segment, which experts believe will drive around 40% of segment profit by fiscal 2027.

“It (HPE) has more than doubled its networking purchase commitments, while the company's total binding purchase obligations, mostly related to inventory, have reached roughly nine times their level at the end of FY25,” Seeking Alpha analyst Vishal Jadaun said.

The company upped the growth outlook of the networking business to the high teens to low 20s in FY27 and margins to the mid-to-high 20s, Jadaun added.

Moreover, Citi analysts also noted that the quarter could be positive for shareholders, with management targeting a resumption of share buybacks in F4Q.

“With management targeting a return to buybacks in F4Q, supported by strong FCF generation, we see an attractive shareholder return profile,” Asiya Merchant said.

Over the last 2 years, HPE has beaten EPS estimates 88% of the time and has beaten revenue estimates 75% of the time.

data.title: Flight to safety drives Treasury yields lower as tech tumbles
data.description:
U.S. Treasury yields declined across the curve on Friday afternoon as equity markets came under pressure, prompting investors to shift into government bonds for relative safety.

The move reflected a classic flight-to-quality response. With stocks selling off, demand for Treasuries increased, driving yields lower.

The front end of the curve led the decline: the U.S. 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y)  fell 11 basis points to 4.65%, the largest drop among the major maturities. The benchmark U.S. 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) dropped 10 basis points to 4.94%, while the longer-end U.S. 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) eased 7 basis points to 5.33%.

The coordinated retreat underscored heightened caution among market participants. Bond purchases accelerated as equity losses mounted, tightening yields, especially in shorter-dated paper that is more sensitive to near-term shifts in risk appetite and rate expectations.

The session illustrated the ongoing interplay between equities and fixed income. When stock prices weaken, Treasuries frequently absorb the resulting capital flows, producing the inverse relationship observed Friday.

data.title: RLX signals “transitional working capital absorption” from U.K. excise duty while maintaining “minimum payout ratio of 100%”
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: RLX Technology (RLX) Q3 2026

Management View

  • “The third quarter marked an inflection point for RLX.” (Chief Financial Officer Chao Lu)

  • “Net revenues reached RMB 1.92 billion, our highest quarterly total since the second quarter of 2022.” (Chief Financial Officer Chao Lu) He added, “International business accounted for 86.5% of total net revenue,” and said the growth was “primarily driven by the consolidation of our newly acquired Western European distribution business this past July.” (Chief Financial Officer Lu)

  • “Having direct connection to over 30,000 physical retail endpoints and the proprietary B2B ordering platform connecting more than 20,000 independent merchants gives us a clear firsthand understanding of what retailers need and what products actually drive sell-through at the store level.” (Chief Financial Officer Lu)

  • “Gross margin was 23.3%, an expected normalization reflecting the structural shift in our business mix following the July consolidation as distribution businesses inherently operate at a lower gross margin than branded products.” (Chief Financial Officer Lu)

  • “Supported by this financial flexibility, we remain unwavering in our commitment to shareholder return, maintaining a minimum payout ratio of 100% of non-GAAP net income through regular dividends and ongoing share repurchases.” (Chief Financial Officer Lu)

  • No CEO prepared remarks were included in this quarter’s transcript; prepared remarks were delivered by the CFO.

Outlook

  • “Looking ahead, the U.K. introduction of excise duty in October is expected to result in transitional working capital absorption over the coming quarters.” (Chief Financial Officer Chao Lu)

  • “With our financial strength, compliance capability, localized field execution, and direct channel reach, RLX is uniquely positioned to capture market share and deliver sustain -- sustainable long-term value to our shareholders.” (Chief Financial Officer Lu)

  • “Following year-end settlements, management and the Board will evaluate a dividend in the first half of next year, upholding our commitment to return at least 100% of our non-GAAP net income annually through both dividends and share repurchases.” (Head of Capital Markets Sam Tsang)

  • “As existing inventory cycles through on a first-in, first-out basis, we expect these operational synergies to drive meaningful margin expansion next year.” (Head of Capital Markets Tsang)

Financial Results

  • “Net revenues reached RMB 1.92 billion.” (Chief Financial Officer Chao Lu)

  • “Gross profit increased 26.7% year-over-year and 24.8% sequentially to RMB 446.6 million.” (Chief Financial Officer Lu)

  • “Total operating expenses were RMB 407.1 million compared with RMB 259.3 million in the same period of 2025.” (Chief Financial Officer Lu)

  • “Non-GAAP income from operations was RMB 143.8 million, and non-GAAP net income reached RMB 235.6 million.” (Chief Financial Officer Lu)

  • “Net cash generated from operating activities rebounded to RMB 40.0 million, returning to positive territory following an operating cash flow outflow of RMB 63.2 million last quarter.” (Chief Financial Officer Lu)

  • “Our total financial assets, including cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash, and short- and long-term deposits and investments stood at RMB 13.48 billion or approximately USD 2.01 billion.” (Chief Financial Officer Lu)

Q&A

  • Christine Peng, UBS Investment Bank, Research Division: asked how RLX balances M&A with shareholder returns and the impact of China VAT rebate changes; Head of Capital Markets Tsang said “our GAAP gross margin in the third quarter was weighted down by RMB 43.5 million of a onetime noncash cost of revenue adjustment” and added on VAT rebates that “The net impact of our core operating margins remains minimal.” (Head of Capital Markets Tsang)

  • Lydia Ling, Citigroup Inc., Research Division: asked for 2027 international expansion outlook, European market share plan/challenges, and M&A pipeline; Head of Capital Markets Tsang said “heading into 2027, our international growth builds directly on this foundation by pairing global standard, Shenzhen Speed product engineering with strong local commercial execution,” and added “we maintain a robust M&A pipeline centered primarily on Europe.” (Head of Capital Markets Tsang)

  • Yuying Zou, China International Capital Corporation Limited, Research Division: asked about Southeast Asia strategy and the July European acquisition integration/profitability; Head of Capital Markets Tsang said “across Southeast Asia, RLX holds a #1 market leadership in multiple key countries,” and on Europe added “we completed the financial integration in the third quarter,” with profitability expectations that “we expect these operational synergies to drive meaningful margin expansion next year.” (Head of Capital Markets Tsang)

  • Yun Guo, Citic Securities Co., Ltd., Research Division: asked about U.K. e-liquid tax impact and RLX strategy; Head of Capital Markets Tsang called the duty “a constructive long-term catalyst for the compliant sector” and said “full pricing and market dynamics should become more visible towards the end of first quarter next year.” (Head of Capital Markets Tsang)

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was neutral to slightly skeptical, concentrating on capital allocation trade-offs, regulatory changes, and profitability visibility from the European consolidation (e.g., Christine Peng asked whether M&A “could depress the earnings”). (Christine Peng, UBS Investment Bank, Research Division)

  • Management tone was slightly positive and positioning-focused, using conviction language around compliance and share gains, while acknowledging near-term frictions (e.g., “expected to result in transitional working capital absorption”). (Chief Financial Officer Chao Lu)

  • Versus last quarter, management messaging shifted from preparing investors for the Q3 consolidation to highlighting it as executed (“inflection point”), while analysts continued pressing on capital allocation and margins, now with more emphasis on integration and tax pass-through mechanics.

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Q3 emphasized that “these initiatives came together as one for the first time integrated global platform,” while Q2 framed the same strategy as groundwork, including “expanding through capital-efficient strategic partnerships and equity investments” and that the Western Europe entity “will be fully consolidated… starting in the third quarter of 2026.” (Chief Financial Officer Chao Lu; Co-founder, Chairperson of the Board of Directors & CEO Wang Ying; Chief Financial Officer Chao Lu)

  • The prepared-remarks leadership changed from Q2, where CEO Wang delivered the opening, to Q3, where CFO Lu led prepared remarks and positioning language around the “integrated global platform.”

  • Margin narrative moved from Q2’s “gross margin expanded… to 35.4%” tied to mix and optimization to Q3’s “gross margin was 23.3%” described as mix normalization from distribution consolidation. (Chief Financial Officer Chao Lu)

Risks and Concerns

  • “Foreign currency depreciation against the RMB directly reduces our translated RMB revenue while our RMB cost base stays unchanged,” which management described as “a passive translation headwind on reported revenue and gross margin rather than any underlying weakness in our business.” (Chief Financial Officer Chao Lu)

  • “The U.K. introduction of excise duty in October is expected to result in transitional working capital absorption,” and management also noted a market transition period through March. (Chief Financial Officer Chao Lu)

  • Acquisition-related accounting and integration items were highlighted, including “RMB 43.5 million of a onetime noncash cost of revenue adjustment” tied to inventory fair value step-up. (Head of Capital Markets Sam Tsang)

Final Takeaway

Management described Q3 as the quarter RLX’s international expansion and Western Europe distribution consolidation first operated as an “integrated global platform,” with results reflecting a larger international revenue mix and lower percentage gross margin tied to distribution economics. Management reiterated a shareholder-return framework of a “minimum payout ratio of 100% of non-GAAP net income” via dividends and buybacks, while flagging near-term factors investors are likely to watch—U.K. excise-duty-driven working-capital absorption, FX translation headwinds in RMB reporting, and the pace of margin improvement from European integration synergies expected “next year.”

data.title: Markets were overdue for a tech correction, but trade will bounce – JPMorgan’s David Kelly
data.description:
The stock market was overdue for a tech (XLK) correction, according to David Kelly, JPMorgan Asset Management's chief global strategist, who pointed to Nvidia's (NVDA) recent problems and broader technological disruptions as key factors driving the pullback.

In an interview with CNBC, Kelly noted that the troubles have been "rattling a few people."

Despite concerns about the AI trade and slowing demand in the tech sector (VGT), (XLK), Kelly sees inflation pressures easing and little evidence of broad economic overheating.

He expects falling gasoline prices (XB1:COM) alone will reduce the year-over-year increase in CPI by four-tenths of a percent for November.

"I see no evidence that in the big, broad economy outside of tech, there's that strong demand," Kelly said, pointing to flat new housing activity and weak consumer basics.

On Federal Reserve policy, Kelly pushed back against expectations for aggressive rate hikes. He characterized Fed Governor Waller as "a lonesome poke" in his support for a 50-basis-point hike, saying he does not believe the majority of Federal Reserve officials share that view.

Kelly anticipates a move in December followed by a pause rather than continued tightening.

He also argued that markets are constructing a hawkish Fed narrative in the absence of forward guidance, but he sees no justification for aggressive action.

"With rates already as pretty close to neutral levels, there's no reason for the Federal Reserve to be aggressive here," he said.

Looking ahead, Kelly expressed optimism about market resilience. He noted that steady inflows through 401(k) contributions, stock buybacks, and purchases by wealthy Americans provide consistent support.

"Unless you have a big reason for negativity, chances are this market will bounce," he said.

Tech ETFs: (VGT), (XLK), (IYW), (FTEC), (IXN), and (RSPT).

data.title: Noisy quarter, louder rally: Buy-side optimism trumps sell-side caution at Gap
data.description:
It was a noisy quarter for Gap (GAP): earnings, inflated by tariffs, beat estimates; revenue rose just 2%; and gross margin missed expectations as warmer-than-expected weather early in the quarter drove heavier promotions at Old Navy and Athleta.

Shares continue to rally, however, as the downward revision to FY26 was less than feared given the poor performance of Athleta and Banana Republic, and a new brand president for Athleta brings hope that the worst is over for its perpetually underperforming brand. 

“This was a soft result but comes against what we perceive to be low investor expectations,” Goldman Sachs’ Brooke Roache noted. She was encouraged by the sequential improvement at Old Navy and the continued healthy trends at Gap but warns that Old Navy remains a “show-me story until the company demonstrates a return to positive and consistent comp trends.”

The performance among the four banners was also mixed, with positive comparable sales at Gap and flat at Old Navy against negative comps at Banana Republic and Athleta. Management blamed Banana Republic’s weakness on a disproportionate assortment in women’s cold weather apparel and conceded that Athleta’s comps are expected to be more challenged in Q4.

But while the Gap’s (GAP) share performance on Friday points to investor confidence, analysts are less convinced in an inflection in comparable store sales for Banana Republic and Athleta.

“Without a clearer path to positive revisions, we see limited scope for meaningful multiple expansion in the next twelve months,” said Morgan Stanley’s Alex Straton, who maintains her Equal-weight rating on the stock.

Wells Fargo’s Ike Boruchow is also keeping his Equal Weight rating, “despite the Gap brand still working.”

“Reaccelerating the Old Navy business could take several quarters, given historical precedents and rising concerns about value-consumers.”

Goldman’s Roach agrees and believes further improvement in Old Navy will be necessary to drive stock outperformance from here, while early Q4 trends are “weighing on the timeline for delivery.”

The sell-side caution is doing little to dent buy-side optimism with Gap (GAP) shares erasing last week’s losing streak that wiped out 16% of the stock’s value.

data.title: Microsoft draws mixed signals as hedge funds reshuffle positions in Q3
data.description:
Hedge fund positioning in Microsoft (MSFT) was mixed in Q3 2026, with several prominent investors initiating new positions while others reduced or exited existing holdings. The activity points to differing views on the software and cloud computing giant.

The most notable new positions included Third Point, led by Dan Loeb, which initiated a position of approximately 450,000 Microsoft shares. Soros Capital, led by Robert Soros, also opened a new position of 954 shares, while Thiel Macro, led by Peter Thiel, initiated a smaller stake of 2,000 shares. Discovery Capital, led by Rob Citrone, likewise established a new position of about 46,000 shares.

On the other hand, Pershing Square, led by Bill Ackman, reduced its Microsoft holdings by ~35%, from 6.21M shares to 4.06M shares. Altimeter Capital Management, led by Brad Gerstner, reduced its Microsoft exposure during Q3, cutting its holdings by approximately 7% to 1.18M shares from 1.27M shares. Soros Fund, led by George Soros, also trimmed its position, lowering its holdings from approximately 190,000 shares to 122,000 shares. 

Viking Global, led by Andreas Halvorsen, took a more decisive step, exiting its Microsoft position entirely after holding approximately 1.46M shares in the previous quarter. The full exit represents one of the more notable institutional departures from the stock during Q3. Corvex Management, led by Keith Meister, also exited its 132,000-share position entirely.

Some prominent investors maintained their exposure. Tiger Global, led by Chase Coleman, held ~2.27M Microsoft shares unchanged during the quarter.
